These are this winter’s train times

Train companies change their timetables twice a year, and the summer one is not the same as the winter one. Some trains run at different times, and a few get added or taken away. A change that works well now may not work in summer.

Every time on this page comes from a winter weekend, so please treat it as a guide to how the trains run. When I last checked, the summer 2027 times had not been published. They usually come out in the spring, and I will update this page when they do. I have kept to the trains and changes that work well, so a journey planner may show a few more options.

          Before you travel

          Pay less to get there

          Ways I have found to bring the cost of the trip down

          Book Advance tickets early

          An Advance ticket is often the cheapest way to go, but it ties you to one train. I would pick the train you want first, then book. They can sell out, so book as soon as the show dates are out.

          Train
          Think about an off peak ticket

          An off peak ticket lets you choose the train on the day, which suits a show when you do not know when you will want to go home. Check the time rules on the ticket before you buy.

          Train
          Look at a railcard

          A Family and Friends Railcard takes a third off adult fares and 60% off children’s fares, and it can pay for itself in one trip. Two Together, Senior, 16 to 25, 26 to 30 and Disabled Persons railcards all give a third off too.

          Railcard

          Good to know

          Quick answers before you travel.

          Which station is closest to the show?
          Headcorn. The aerodrome is about 1.5 miles from the station, so I would take a taxi or allow about 30 minutes on foot. Staplehurst is the next station along towards London, but it is further away, so I would stick with Headcorn.
          How do I get from the station to the aerodrome?
          Taxis are available from the station, and on show days I would book one ahead, as there are not many in a small village. The number 12 bus is another option, as it runs from the station to the Aerodrome stop. If you fancy the walk, it is around 30 minutes through the village and out to the aerodrome, so wear comfy shoes. I would also check the show website nearer the time in case a shuttle bus is laid on.
          Do I need a ticket for the show?
          Yes. 2027 tickets are on sale on the official Headcorn Airshow website, and I would book them before you travel.
          When is the show?
          The 2027 show is on Saturday 26 and Sunday 27 June, with a Futures and Arrivals Day on the Friday. The times on this page are a guide from this winter’s timetable, as the summer one is not out yet.
          What if my train is late or cancelled?
          Look at the live board above or the National Rail app before you leave the house. On a flexible ticket you can usually take the next train. With an Advance ticket, speak to the staff at the station.
          I am coming from further away. What do I do?
          I only show Southeastern trains on this page, so I would plan your trip to whichever of the twelve stations here is nearest to you, and pick it up from there. From most of London, that will be Charing Cross, Waterloo East or London Bridge.

          Travelling with a disability or a buggy

          Trains can work really well for an airshow, as long as you plan the step free parts before you leave.

          • Book Passenger Assist on the National Rail app or by phone, and staff will meet you at the train.
          • Check the station has step free access to every platform you need, both ways.
